subject: dsa
title: Meeting Rooms
summary: You can attend every meeting only if none overlap. Sort by start time, then compare each meeting with the next: if one starts before the previous ends, there's a conflict and the answer is false.
problem: Given meeting time intervals, determine whether a single person could attend all of them.

steps.caption: You can attend every meeting only if no two overlap. First sort the meetings by start time so any clash shows up between neighbors.
Compare each meeting with the next. The first runs from 0 to 30, while the next starts at 5, before the first one ends.
Since 5 < 30, these two meetings overlap; you'd have to be in both at once.
A single overlap is enough to decide it: you cannot attend all the meetings, so the answer is false.
